apps.name: TB Frontend (React SPA)
apps.techStack: React 18 + TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, React Flow

findings.name: Sheet grid (canonical sortable/filterable list)
findings.plainSummary: Every list screen (Roles, Tasks, Standards, Applications) uses one shared spreadsheet-style grid, so all lists look and behave identically.

findings.name: Header combobox filters with cascading options
findings.plainSummary: Each grid column header contains a searchable dropdown whose choices automatically narrow to match the other active filters, like Excel.

findings.name: Column picker with hide/reorder/resize
findings.plainSummary: Users can show, hide, reorder, and resize grid columns, and their layout is remembered per user.

findings.name: Inspector drill-down sidebar
findings.plainSummary: One shared side panel shows everything connected to a process step — roles, applications, deliverables, tasks, and governance — in tabs.

findings.name: DrawerShell modal drawer frame
findings.plainSummary: A single reusable slide-out drawer frame gives every detail popup the same look, dimmed backdrop, and close behavior.

findings.name: In-app confirm/prompt dialog system
findings.plainSummary: All confirmations and prompts use the app's own styled dialogs — including type-the-name confirmation for dangerous deletes — never raw browser popups.

findings.name: StatusPill tone-mapped status badges
findings.plainSummary: Statuses everywhere render as small color-coded pills drawn from one shared component, so green always means the same thing.

findings.name: Button / LinkButton component pair
findings.plainSummary: All buttons and button-styled links come from one shared component so actions look consistent on every screen.

findings.name: Shared form field kit (Input/Select/Textarea/Label)
findings.plainSummary: Forms across the app compose from one shared set of text boxes, dropdowns, and labels rather than each page inventing its own.

findings.name: Empty / loading / error / skeleton states
findings.plainSummary: Every screen shows the same polished placeholders while data loads, when a list is empty, or when something goes wrong.

findings.name: Sidebar navigation derived from the shared menu registry
findings.plainSummary: The left navigation is generated from the same menu list the server uses for permissions, so users only see tabs they are allowed to open.

findings.name: Non-blocking feedback panel with silent screenshot
findings.plainSummary: Users can write feedback in a side panel while still using the page, and a screenshot of what they were looking at is attached automatically on submit.

findings.name: Home dashboard widget catalog
findings.plainSummary: The Home page is assembled from a catalog of dashboard widgets that admins can add, remove, and reorder per company without code changes.

findings.name: Workspace rationalization board (React Flow)
findings.plainSummary: The Workspace tab draws each application's process stages and layer-by-layer findings as an interactive board users can rearrange.

findings.name: AI-adoption mode vocabulary (labels only, content in DB)
findings.plainSummary: The four AI autonomy levels are defined once as labels in code while the actual per-stream adoption content lives in the database where admins edit it.

findings.name: Route-level code splitting (lazy pages)
findings.plainSummary: Each page's code is downloaded only when the user first visits it, keeping the initial app load fast.
findings.codeRef: frontend/src/App.tsx : React.lazy per page behind one Suspense

findings.name: RouteGuard client-side access mirror
findings.plainSummary: If someone deep-links to a tab they can't access, the app redirects them to their start page instead of showing a broken screen — the server remains the real gatekeeper.

findings.name: Debounced auto-save preference store
findings.plainSummary: Layout choices like column setups and dashboard arrangements apply instantly on screen and are quietly saved to the user's profile moments later.

findings.name: Excel-style cascading filter recomputation
findings.plainSummary: As filters are applied, every other dropdown instantly recalculates which choices still make sense, and stale picks clear themselves.

findings.name: User-curated board overlay persistence
findings.plainSummary: When a user drags boxes or redraws arrows on the Workspace board, only their changes are saved as a thin overlay on top of the generated layout.

findings.name: Oversized Workspace page module (781 lines)
findings.plainSummary: The Workspace board page has grown to roughly 1.5 times the codebase's own 500-line file limit, making it the hardest screen to maintain.

findings.name: Single fetch wrapper with /api prefix + auth header
findings.plainSummary: All server calls funnel through one small client that adds the sign-in token and the right address automatically.

findings.name: GET promise cache with dedupe
findings.plainSummary: Revisiting a screen shows its data instantly from memory instead of re-downloading it, and duplicate simultaneous requests are collapsed into one.

findings.name: Write-through cache invalidation
findings.plainSummary: Any time the user saves a change, the app throws away its cached lists so the next read is guaranteed fresh — except rapid-fire preference saves, which skip the wipe.

findings.name: Nav-hover prefetch
findings.plainSummary: Hovering over a navigation item quietly starts downloading that tab's data, so the click feels instant.

findings.name: 401 session-expiry redirect
findings.plainSummary: If the sign-in expires, the app clears the stale session and returns the user to the login page instead of showing errors.

findings.name: Throttled 403 permission re-sync
findings.plainSummary: If an admin revokes a permission mid-session, the first blocked request triggers one quiet refresh of what the user is allowed to see.

findings.name: useApi typed GET hook
findings.plainSummary: Read-only pages use one small hook that handles loading spinners, error messages, and refetching the same way everywhere.

findings.name: Lens token-matching of stage names to process tree
findings.plainSummary: The Workspace guesses which business process each rationalization stage belongs to by comparing words in their names, and this guessing logic runs inside the browser page.
findings.rationale: Semantic name-matching is a business rule compensating for a missing foreign key between stages and the process tree; it belongs server-side (or better, as a stored association), not in UI code.

findings.name: Agent-automatability scoring math client-side
findings.plainSummary: The rule for what counts as an 'automatable' task (score 1 or 2 of 5) and the percentage rollups are calculated in the browser rather than by the server.
findings.rationale: The automatability threshold is a business definition (defect A-02 decision); computing it client-side means any other consumer (API, exports, reports) can disagree with the screen.

findings.name: Stage lifecycle vocabulary duplicated client-side
findings.plainSummary: The list of initiative stages (Idea, Plan, Execute, Complete) is written out twice — once in the browser code and once in the server's approval engine — so they can drift apart.
findings.rationale: A lifecycle vocabulary maintained in two codebases is reference data; it should live once in the shared package or a reference table.

findings.name: CAPDAN/layer vocabulary duplicated across apps
findings.plainSummary: The five IT layers and the Common/Different/Relocate/Eliminate categories are defined separately in the browser code and the server code instead of once in a shared place.
findings.rationale: Two hand-maintained copies of the same classification vocabulary invite drift; the shared workspace package exists precisely for this.

findings.name: Raw role-string checks in User Admin screens
findings.plainSummary: The User Admin screens decide what to show by checking the raw account type text ('SITE_ADMIN') instead of asking the shared permission system.
findings.rationale: The codebase's own convention is to derive capability from the effective-permission service, never from role string equality; these checks bypass that abstraction (server enforcement still applies).

findings.name: Data dictionary content hard-coded in frontend
findings.plainSummary: The plain-language glossary shown in the Data Dictionary is authored directly inside the app's code, so fixing a definition requires a software release.
findings.rationale: Authored reference content belongs in the database like the AI-adoption profiles that were already migrated out of code (see aiAdoption.ts header).

findings.name: Feature-module routers with per-router middleware stack
findings.plainSummary: Each feature area (portfolio, explorer, inspector, users) is its own router that applies sign-in, permission, and caching checks once at the top.

findings.name: Inline zod validation at the API boundary
findings.plainSummary: Every incoming request body is checked against a strict schema before any business logic runs, rejecting malformed data early.

findings.name: Shared zod contract package (@cascade/shared)
findings.plainSummary: The server's validation rules and the browser's form types come from the same shared definitions, so both sides always agree on what valid data looks like.

findings.name: requireAuth JWT verification middleware
findings.plainSummary: Every request must carry a valid signed token; the user is re-checked against the database so a deleted or deactivated account is locked out immediately.

findings.name: Tenant-keyed GET response cache with write invalidation
findings.plainSummary: Heavy read endpoints remember their finished answers briefly per customer, and any write anywhere clears the memory so answers are never stale after a change.

findings.name: Central error handler with full request context
findings.plainSummary: Route code passes failures to one central handler that logs the full context and returns a consistent error shape to the browser.

findings.name: Gzip compression of MB-scale JSON payloads
findings.plainSummary: Large data responses are compressed about ten-fold before crossing the network, which is most of what makes big tabs load fast.

findings.name: Webhook HMAC signature over raw bytes
findings.plainSummary: Incoming user-provisioning messages from the identity system must carry a cryptographic signature computed over the exact bytes sent, blocking forged or tampered payloads.

findings.name: Webhook idempotency ledger
findings.plainSummary: Each identity-system event is recorded by its unique ID so replays and retries can never create duplicate users, and unfixable bad payloads are not retried forever.

findings.name: Feedback pipeline checkpoint-and-resume
findings.plainSummary: Feedback delivery (generate ticket, file it in Jira, attach screenshot, notify) checkpoints each step, so a retry resumes where it failed and can never file the same ticket twice.

findings.name: Health endpoint with live DB probe
findings.plainSummary: A health check confirms the database actually answers and reports which code version is deployed.

findings.name: 404-not-403 cross-tenant policy
findings.plainSummary: Requests for another customer's records answer 'not found' rather than 'forbidden', so outsiders can't even confirm a record exists.

findings.name: ancestorNames location resolver
findings.plainSummary: A record's location labels (value stream, domain, division, department) are computed on demand from the hierarchy instead of being copied onto dozens of tables.

findings.name: Resolver suite (roles/apps/subtree/counts/link names)
findings.plainSummary: One shared toolkit answers all cross-connection questions — which roles, apps, and structures relate to a process — so no screen re-invents the traversal.
findings.codeRef: backend/src/lib/resolvers/index.ts : rolesForNodes, appsForNodes, processSubtree, structureCounts, linkNames

findings.name: Governance rollups from task-grain links
findings.plainSummary: Standards and regulations are recorded once at the most detailed task level, and every higher-level view is calculated upward from there — nothing is stored twice.

findings.name: Batch-load + in-memory aggregation pattern
findings.plainSummary: List endpoints fetch related records in a few bulk queries and assemble the answer in memory, avoiding the slow one-query-per-row trap.
findings.codeRef: backend/src/routes/work.ts : single {in: ids} junction loads + ancestorNames batch

findings.name: Initiative financial rollup recompute
findings.plainSummary: An initiative's cumulative benefit, cost, and net impact are recalculated from its detailed time-phased figures whenever those change.

findings.name: Stage-gate approval engine
findings.plainSummary: Initiatives move through Idea, Plan, Execute, and Complete via submit/approve/move-back actions, with every action recorded in the audit log.

findings.name: Effective-permission resolution service
findings.plainSummary: What each user may see and do is computed in one place by merging their user-type grants with any individual overrides across the menu tree.

findings.name: Data-health check suite
findings.plainSummary: A read-only battery of checks scans the data for drift and inconsistencies and points admins at the exact offending rows, without ever changing data itself.
findings.codeRef: backend/src/services/validations.ts : Check runners for the Data Health panel

findings.name: Rationalization progress math server-side
findings.plainSummary: Migration progress percentages and category counts for the Workspace board are computed by the server from each finding's lifecycle status.

findings.name: Free-text role name fuzzy matching (roleMatch)
findings.plainSummary: Workbook rows name their responsible roles as plain text, so the server guesses which real role is meant using abbreviation expansion and name normalization on every read.
findings.rationale: IoItem and ProcessStep tie to roles only by comma-separated name strings — the schema's own rule is 'no free-text cross-references'; these should be proper foreign-key links, eliminating the runtime guessing.

findings.name: Generic typed-graph data model (erd_v5)
findings.plainSummary: Everything in the operating model — processes, roles, standards, apps — is stored as entities wired together by explicit link tables, never as loose text references.

findings.name: Closure tables for hierarchy ancestry
findings.plainSummary: Pre-built ancestor/descendant lookup tables let the app answer 'what rolls up where' in one query instead of walking the tree step by step.

findings.name: Migrations-only schema policy with squashed baseline
findings.plainSummary: Every database structure change goes through a recorded, replayable migration — ad-hoc schema pushes are banned after a past incident silently dropped columns.
findings.codeRef: backend/prisma/migrations/0_baseline : ADR-001 squash; vercel-build runs prisma migrate deploy

findings.name: Row-per-key user preference store
findings.plainSummary: Each saved user preference is its own small database row, so rapid auto-saves touch only the key that changed.

findings.name: Denormalized cumulative rollup columns
findings.plainSummary: Initiative totals are stored on the record for fast reading and are refreshed by a single recompute routine whenever the underlying figures change.

findings.name: File-based feedback pipeline config
findings.plainSummary: The feedback feature's switches and Jira target live in a small settings file that can be edited without redeploying, while all secrets stay in the environment.

findings.name: Shared menu registry as the entitlement spine
findings.plainSummary: One master list of tabs and sub-tabs drives navigation, route guards, and permission enforcement on both the browser and server sides.

findings.name: Enum token lists living only in schema comments
findings.plainSummary: Many database fields have their allowed values (like High/Medium/Low or manual/augmented/automated) written only as code comments, with nothing actually enforcing them.
findings.recommendedLayer: Data (reference tables or shared validated constants)
findings.rationale: Allowed-value lists documented as comments are unenforced reference data; a typo'd token inserts cleanly and silently breaks filters and rollups.

findings.name: Geography list hard-coded in shared constants
findings.plainSummary: The list of operating geographies (North America, UK/Europe, APAC, LATAM) is baked into the code, so adding a region requires releasing both apps.
findings.rationale: Geographies are business reference data that will change; unlike the user-type contract, nothing architectural requires them to be compile-time constants.

findings.name: Hard-coded demo password in seed scripts
findings.plainSummary: Every seeded demo account, including the admin, shares the same password written directly into the source code.
findings.rationale: A shared credential checked into source is acceptable only for throwaway demos; it should come from an environment variable so a seeded production-adjacent branch never ships a known password.

findings.name: Deterministic synthetic demo metrics
findings.plainSummary: Demo metric values are generated with a repeatable hash-based jitter so seeded environments look realistic but identical on every rebuild, and are flagged as illustrative.

findings.name: Pino structured logging with request correlation IDs
findings.plainSummary: Every request is logged with its method, duration, status, and customer, plus a unique ID echoed back to the browser so any issue can be traced end to end.

findings.name: requirePermission menu-key CRUD gate
findings.plainSummary: Each feature's API is wrapped by one guard that maps the request type (read, create, update, delete) to the user's granted permissions for that tab.

findings.name: Domain-admin ABAC org-subtree scoping
findings.plainSummary: Department-level admins can only manage users inside their own branch of the organization, and the system fails closed if that branch can't be found.

findings.name: JWT session tokens (7-day expiry)
findings.plainSummary: Sign-ins are cryptographically signed tokens that expire after a week and never carry permissions, so revoked access can't hide inside an old token.

findings.name: Silent 'dev-secret' JWT fallback
findings.plainSummary: If the signing secret is missing from the environment, the server quietly falls back to a publicly known placeholder instead of refusing to start.
findings.rationale: A misconfigured production deploy would sign every session with a secret anyone can read in the repo; the server should fail fast when JWT_SECRET is absent.

findings.name: API keys hashed at rest, shown once
findings.plainSummary: Integration keys are displayed to the admin exactly once at creation; only a one-way fingerprint is stored, so a database leak reveals no usable keys.

findings.name: Deactivated-account kill-switch
findings.plainSummary: Deactivating a user cuts off their access on their very next request, even though their sign-in token would otherwise remain technically valid for days.

findings.name: Audit trail with field-level diffs
findings.plainSummary: Every meaningful change records who did what to which record, including exactly which fields changed from what to what.

findings.name: console.error escape hatch in the audit service
findings.plainSummary: When writing an audit record fails, the failure is reported through a raw console print that bypasses the structured logging every other part of the server uses.
findings.rationale: The repo's own rule is 'never console.log in backend src' — audit-write failures are exactly the events that must land in the structured pino stream where they can be alerted on.

findings.name: Open CORS behind a same-origin proxy
findings.plainSummary: The API accepts requests from any origin by design, because it is only reachable through the app's own front door and every route still demands a valid sign-in.

findings.name: Vercel two-service routing with /api prefix strip
findings.plainSummary: In production one platform serves both the website and the API, routing anything under /api to the server with the prefix removed — mirroring how local development works.

findings.name: Legacy requireRole gate alongside the permission service
findings.plainSummary: A handful of site-admin-only surfaces (company deletion, feedback admin, API keys) are still guarded by direct role checks rather than the newer permission system, creating two parallel access mechanisms.
findings.codeRef: backend/src/middleware/auth.ts : requireRole (used in routes/companies.ts:79, routes/feedback.ts:105, routes/users/apiKeys.ts:17)
findings.rationale: The rest of the API migrated to requirePermission over the shared menu tree; the surviving raw-role gates should resolve through the same effective-permission service so access rules live in one place.
